subject.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)

question: Should OpenClaw’s shared persisted-history and visible-text sanitizers treat every standalone `antml:`/`mm:` invoke block or `<function_calls>`-wrapped invoke block as leaked tool-call data, while preserving bare invoke XML as user content?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but this is a cross-channel policy choice that irreversibly removes qualified text from durable history and cannot be settled by unit coverage alone.

options.title: Adopt the qualified-leak boundary
options.body: Merge the current narrow allow-list because the known proxy degradation carries a namespace or wrapper signature and bare examples remain preserved.

options.title: Limit removal to delivery only
options.body: Keep persisted transcripts verbatim and strip qualified markup only from user-facing delivery if maintainers prefer retaining all raw history evidence.

options.title: Pause for a provider-contract decision
options.body: Hold the PR if the team wants a broader provider-owned classification or an execution-recovery path before standardizing sanitizer behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt the qualified-leak boundary
recommendation.body: Merge the current narrow allow-list because the known proxy degradation carries a namespace or wrapper signature and bare examples remain preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans shared runtime text policy and durable transcript semantics rather than only the contributor’s proposed repair.
